title: Throughput guarantee matrix, degradation allowance, and incident credit computation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a compact, legally-clear matrix that maps committed dedicated capacity to measurable throughput bands, explicit degradation allowances, and a transparent incident credit formula. This ticket produces the canonical document and contract-ready snippets for sales and legal: a) service guarantee matrix (banded throughput expectations vs. windows), b) definition of measured failures and 'degradation events', c) the error-budgeting model and credit computation, and d) the operational remediation and escalation workflow for customers on Dedicated plans.
acceptance_criteria: A clear matrix (CSV and human-readable table) that ties committed GPU pools and qps/token targets to quantile-based measurement windows
Definitions for "degradation event" and "partial degradation" that are precise enough for billing/legal review
A tested credit formula that references observable metrics from Console (per-route served_tokens, 99th/95th quantiles) with worked examples and edge-case handling
Legal-approved contract snippets (3 variations: standard, enterprise, air-gapped) for inclusion in MSA and order forms
Integration notes for telemetry and SLI mapping (eng teams sign-off) and a playbook for customer-facing remediation steps
progress_updates: 2025-11-22: Kickoff meeting with Legal, Sales, and Runtime SRE. Agreed on goal: shorten dispute resolution by defining deterministic measurement windows.
2025-12-08: Drafted initial banding matrix (bands: Premium, Standard, Economy) and shared with Sales for pricing alignment. Feedback: want deterministic credits rather than discretionary credits.
2026-01-15: Eng provided telemetry mapping: per-tenant token counts, request latencies, and availability events. Confirmed ability to compute per-az quantiles and aggregate across pools.
2026-02-02: Legal requested explicit definitions for customer-triggered vs platform-caused degradations. Added section listing customer responsibilities (e.g., client retries, malformed requests).
2026-02-20: Ran simulation on last 6 months of production traffic to validate credit formula; estimated median monthly credits for minor degradations <1% of revenue. Adjusted thresholds accordingly.
2026-03-05: Draft contract snippets prepared and shared with Sales and Legal. Scheduled 03/12 cross-functional review with SREs for edge cases (network partitions, AZ failover).
review_feedback: Legal: Strip subjective language, replace 'best effort' with quantifiable thresholds and notice windows
Sales: Prefer a simplified two-tier credit approach for SMB customers to avoid negotiation overhead; enterprise customers can keep full banded formula
SRE: Recommend adding automatic temporary capacity boosts (short-term burst) to reduce small-window degradations before applying credits
Finance: Ask to cap monthly credits at contract value and include offsetting remedies (service credits only, not refunds)
decisions: Adopt banded throughput matrix with three bands: Guaranteed, Floor-with-Autoscale, Best-Effort. Each band maps to a measurable quantile for token throughput and a minimum availability percentage.
Credit computation will be deterministic and formulaic: credits = min(contract_monthly_charge, baseline_proportional_credit), with worked examples in the doc.
Customer-triggered degradations (misconfiguration, traffic spikes beyond committed burst, malformed requests) will be excluded from credit calculations when evidence exists.
Implement temporary burst autoscale (engineering ticket ENG-66201) as the preferred first remediation; credits apply only if autoscale did not prevent the degradation or was disabled.
Provide three contract snippets (standard, enterprise, air-gapped) with the same measurement logic but different notice and remediation timelines.
open_questions: Should credits be computed per-tenant or aggregated per-organization for multi-tenant customers with multiple projects? (impact: complexity vs. fairness)
How do we treat mixed-workload customers where embeddings-heavy usage skews token measurements? Need a weighting strategy or separate measurement buckets.
Do we allow post-incident retrospective credits for incidents discovered >90 days after the event? Legal prefers hard windows for dispute closure.
implementation_notes: Telemetry mapping: use Console route-level metrics (served_tokens, requests, errors) with 1-minute granularity, roll to 5m/1h windows for measurement
Measurement windows: 1-hour sliding window for immediate degradations, 30-day window for monthly credit cap calculations
Edge-case handling: network partition across AZs will use region-level aggregation and require incident correlation from SRE incident timeline
Rollout plan: pilot credits with three enterprise customers for 2 months before exposing snippets to general sales team
contract_language_snippets: Standard: "Redwood guarantees the committed throughput band as defined in Exhibit A. If observed throughput for the billing period falls below the guaranteed quantile for the applicable band, Customer will be eligible for Service Credits calculated per the formula in Exhibit B. Service Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy."

Enterprise: "For Enterprise Customers, Redwood will provide the guarantee matrix in Exhibit A and apply the Credit Formula in Exhibit B. Customers may request a post-incident review within 45 days. Credits shall be applied to the next invoice and are subject to the monthly cap."

Air-gapped: "Where Customer operates an air-gapped Private deployment, measurement shall be instrumented by the Customer with metrics exported to Redwood on the agreed telemetry feed. Parties will use the same measurement definitions in Exhibit A and credits will be reconciled per Exhibit B."
compute_credit_formula: Baseline variables: G = guaranteed tokens per-minute (from contract band), O = observed 95th percentile tokens per-minute over measurement window, C = monthly contract charge
Raw shortfall S = max(0, G - O) expressed as percentage of G
Proportional credit P = S * C * adjustment_factor (adjustment_factor defaults to 0.5 for small degradations to avoid over-crediting for transients)
Monthly credit = min(C, sum of P across events in billing period) subject to cap and exclusions
Worked example: Contract month charge = $20,000, G=1,000,000 tokens/day, observed deficit equivalent S=0.08 => P = 0.08 * 20000 * 0.5 = $800.
escalation_playbook: Stage 0: Automated detection — Alerts in Console when quantiles cross threshold; ticket auto-created in SRE queue
Stage 1: SRE triage — 15 minute SLA to acknowledge; attempt autoscale burst and identify customer vs platform cause
Stage 2: Customer outreach — Notify customer within 60 minutes for incidents impacting Guaranteed band; provide mitigation ETA
Stage 3: Post-incident review — Publish timeline and root cause within 72 hours and propose credits within 7 business days
Stage 4: Dispute resolution — If customer disputes measurement, allow 30-day window to submit evidence; final decision by Legal with engineered telemetry as source of truth
qa_plan: Create synthetic workload tests that exercise each band and simulate degradation scenarios (az-failover, kernel OOM, high-embedding ratios)
Verify credit calculation against simulated incident datasets (use last 12 months of anonymized telemetry)
Run end-to-end contract snippet ingestion test: order form -> billing pipeline -> credit issuance
Pilot with two non-critical enterprise customers and collect feedback before general availability
